analysis.answer: Currently, cities have the authority to adopt their own ordinances regulating the sale and possession of firearms. This measure voids all such local ordinances and reserves the power to regulate firearms entirely for the state.

Firearm owners and dealers will no longer need to navigate different regulations when crossing city lines. Cities that wish to restrict firearms more tightly than state law allows will be unable to do so, potentially leading them to seek policy changes at the state legislature instead.

The measure addresses the compliance burden and legal complexity caused by a patchwork of varying local firearm rules. By preempting local laws, it fixes this fragmentation. However, it removes the ability of local governments to address specific municipal safety concerns or localized gun violence with tailored regulations.

The state legislature gains exclusive regulatory power over firearms. City councils and local officials lose their authority to regulate in this area. Gun owners and advocacy groups favoring fewer restrictions benefit from the nullification of local ordinances.
